clue.text: Present key player out of the band

parts.note: B is one of the musical keys

indicators.note: the player comes out of the band, so the band's word stands before the player's

parts.note: a ring is a band, as round a finger
a forward is an attacking player in football or rugby

explanation.surface: Introducing the group's star musician, who has left the band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of the' reverses the clue's order: the player emerges from the band, so the band comes first. 'Key' suggests importance, but it is a musical key.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring forward a proposal is to put it before a meeting, which is to present it.

clue.text: Exclude top man from London borough

parts.note: to bar is to exclude
the king is the top man of a realm

explanation.surface: Banning the boss from a district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: BARKING is a borough in east London.
explanation.definitionFit: Barking, now part of Barking and Dagenham, is a district and former borough of east London.

clue.text: Fibre botanist leaves inside

indicators.note: inside says the letters sit within the words botanist leaves

explanation.surface: A plant scientist leaves the fibres indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Istle is a strong plant fibre from Mexican agave and yucca, used for cord and brushes.

clue.text: Rabelais's giant making Agag turn a somersault?

indicators.note: to turn a somersault is to tumble head over heels, so these letters tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: The giant of French satire flips the Biblical king Agag head over heels.
explanation.walkthrough: Agag is an Amalekite king in the Bible; 'turn a' joins the fodder, and 'somersault' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gargantua is the huge, greedy giant king in Rabelais's sixteenth-century comic novels.

clue.text: Love a girl's shape

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O
Val is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Admiring a young woman's figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An oval is an egg-like geometric outline, an elongated circle.

clue.text: Crushing defeat to a lower formation

indicators.note: formation means the letters of to a lower are formed into a new pattern

explanation.surface: An army is beaten by marching in a lower formation.
explanation.walkthrough: Waterloo was Napoleon's final defeat in 1815; the name now stands for any decisive downfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Meeting one's Waterloo means suffering a final, decisive defeat, after Napoleon's rout in 1815.

clue.text: Part of saint taken by priest in church

indicators.note: in places the priest within the church abbreviation

parts.note: RC is Roman Catholic, a church
Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel

explanation.surface: A fragment of a holy body kept by a cleric in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken by' is a link; Eli is the Old Testament priest who raised Samuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is a bone or other remain of a holy person kept as an object of veneration.

clue.text: Bit of fish for the ballet dancer

definitions.text: Bit of fish for the ballet dancer

parts.words: Bit of fish for the ballet dancer
parts.note: the words read as a fillet of a white fish, but mean the pouch worn at the front of a dancer's costume, historically on hose

explanation.definitionFit: The garment is a padded flap or pouch covering the groin, once on breeches and now jokingly linked to male dancers in tights.

clue.text: This seat gives a rigid driving position

parts.note: set means fixed and rigid
in golf the tee is where one drives from

explanation.surface: A car seat said to give a firm, upright driving posture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driving' suggests a car, but it is a golf drive, struck from the tee.
explanation.definitionFit: A settee is a long upholstered seat for two or more people, a sofa.

clue.text: Checking harangue about trade being ruined

indicators.note: about means going round, so the harangue's word surrounds the rest

parts.note: to rant is to harangue, deliver a loud tirade

indicators.note: trade being ruined has its letters wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A tirade against commerce falling to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Checking' is an adjective here, as in a checking agent; 'being ruined' scrambles 'trade' into ETARD, which 'about' places inside the harangue.
explanation.definitionFit: A retardant substance slows or holds back a process, as fire retardant checks flames.

clue.text: Save game points

parts.note: loo is an old card game
S, south, is a compass point
E, east, is another compass point

explanation.surface: Points rescued in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: LOO is an old gambling card game; 'points' gives two compass points, S and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To loose is to set free or release, as one might save or deliver a captive.

clue.text: Freeze better in Antarctica?

definitions.note: the definition describes what lies in Antarctica, the noun for the polar covering

parts.note: to ice is to freeze
to cap is to better or outdo

explanation.surface: Can anywhere outdo the cold of the South Pole?
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is a verb here, to top or outdo; the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Antarctica is covered by a vast permanent sheet of ice over the land.

clue.text: What an idiot to break a dish

parts.note: to crack is to break
a pot is a dish or vessel

explanation.surface: Only a fool would smash the crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot is a crazy or foolish person, an eccentric with daft ideas.

clue.text: Course for important people

explanation.surface: Studies for VIPs.
explanation.definitionFit: Greats is the Oxford honours degree in classics, a course of study; the greats are also the most eminent figures in a field.

clue.text: Sure can't translate this language

indicators.note: translate means turning the words sure can't into another form, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Certainly no one can translate this ancient tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: Etruscan, of ancient Italy, is famously only partly understood, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Etruscan is the ancient tongue of Etruria in central Italy, still only partly deciphered.

clue.text: Explicit note on the island

parts.note: C is a musical note
Crete is the Greek island

explanation.surface: A clear message written on a Mediterranean isle.
explanation.definitionFit: Concrete means specific and definite, so a concrete proposal is explicit rather than vague.

clue.text: Many pushed forward and got punished

parts.note: C, the Roman numeral for a hundred, stands for many
hastened means hurried or pushed on

explanation.surface: Lots of people hurried on and were disciplined.
explanation.definitionFit: Chastened means disciplined or corrected, made humbler by punishment.

clue.text: Having no bread in Paris but not suffering

parts.note: pain is French for bread
the suffix -less means having no

explanation.surface: Going without bread in France yet not minding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pain' looks English, meaning hurt, which is the surface's trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Painless means causing no hurt, so free from distress.

clue.text: Mundane task takes a time

parts.note: work is a task to be done
a day is a period of time

explanation.surface: A dull chore eats up a whole day.
explanation.definitionFit: Workaday describes the ordinary everyday round, nothing special: ordinary and dull.

clue.text: Waves overwhelm sailor in river

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf, so the waves' word surrounds the sailor's

parts.note: the wash is the waves left by a boat
AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman is swamped by waves in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wabash is a river of Indiana in the American Midwest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wabash is a tributary of the Ohio, flowing through Indiana.

clue.text: Artist arrived first in this privately

definitions.note: a Latin legal phrase meaning 'in the room', used for hearings held in private, is completed by this word

indicators.note: the arrival comes first, so its word stands before the artist's

parts.note: came means arrived
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: The painter got there before anyone in secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts the arrival before the artist. The definition is a fill-in: the legal phrase for a closed hearing is 'in' plus this word.
explanation.definitionFit: A court sitting in private, closed to the public, is said to sit in a judge's chamber, Latin for room.

clue.text: Rebel in girl's school

indicators.note: in puts the rebel inside the girl's name

parts.note: Amy is a girl's name
Jack Cade led a rebellion in Kent in 1450

explanation.surface: An insurgent at a girls' school.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Cade led the 1450 English peasant revolt, a crossword stock rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: An academy is a place of learning, such as a private or specialised college.

clue.text: Disreputable people at a junction in the underground section?

parts.note: base means low or disreputable
men means people
a T is a T-junction, where one road meets another

explanation.surface: Shady characters meet at a crossroads on the Tube.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underground section' suggests the London Underground, but it means part of a house below ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellar storey sits below ground level in a building.

clue.text: Papers, say, end up without an editor

indicators.note: without means outside, so the reversed word goes round the editor
in a down clue up means the word reads from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: an aim is an end or goal
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: Newspapers wind up with no editor.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'up' turns the goal word to MIA; 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: The press, newspapers being an example, make up the mass communication industry.

clue.text: When covering pie, reverse the layers

indicators.note: reverse tells us to read the whole assembly backwards
covering means the word for when goes round the word for pie

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
a tart is a pie

explanation.surface: Instructions for turning over a layered pie once it is covered.
explanation.walkthrough: The assembled word reads ATARTS before 'reverse' turns the whole of it backwards; 'When' for AS is a common crossword substitution.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are beds or levels of rock, one above another, hence layers.

clue.text: A girl can be wrong

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A young woman may err.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiss means awry or faulty, as in something being amiss.

clue.text: Little bit of a feline

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A small piece of a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is the smallest particle of an element, hence a tiny scrap.

clue.text: "Or at the casement see her" (Tennyson)

parts.note: the missing word completes a line from Tennyson's poem The Lady of Shalott, about the lady glimpsed at her window

explanation.walkthrough: The poem asks 'who hath seen her wave her hand? Or at the casement seen her' do what? The blank is the verb for being upright there.
explanation.definitionFit: The line pictures the lady upright at the window; the verb for being on one's feet completes it.

clue.text: Sweeping victory starting to emerge after sixteen moves

indicators.note: the victory and first letter come after the rearranged number
sixteen moves means its letters move about into a new order

parts.note: V stands for victory, as in the V sign

indicators.note: starting to emerge means the first letter of emerge

explanation.surface: A big win begins to appear after sixteen moves of a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves' rearranges 'sixteen' to EXTENSI; 'Sweeping victory' looks like one phrase, but 'Sweeping' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweeping changes are wide-ranging and far-reaching, covering a large area.

clue.text: Some days felt strange mock humility

indicators.note: strange signals that the letters of some days felt are oddly rearranged

explanation.surface: On certain days one felt oddly falsely modest.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretended modesty is a sham show of humbleness, hence mock humility.
